title: Crypto fraud complaints - which agency actually has jurisdiction
p1: Lost money in a crypto scam? The biggest mistake may be assuming there is one agency that handles every crypto fraud complaint.
p2: A crypto transaction does not automatically make the case an "SEBI matter" or a "cybercrime matter." The agency depends on what actually happened.
p3:
If you were tricked through a fake investment platform, wallet, UPI transfer, phishing link or online impersonation, the cybercrime authorities and police may be the starting point for reporting the fraud. If the complaint concerns a regulated securities activity or intermediary, SEBI may have a role. Financial transactions can also bring banks, payment intermediaries or other regulators into the picture.

The useful takeaway: don't choose the authority based only on the word "crypto." Identify the actual misconduct first, then determine which authority has jurisdiction.
conclusion: If someone loses money through a crypto investment scam, which authority do you think they should approach first: the cybercrime police, SEBI, the bank, or someone else?
